name: Invasive Breast Carcinoma, Molecular Subtypes, and Surgical Oncology

reference.source: Sabiston Textbook of Surgery 22nd ed / NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology
clinicalPearls: Breast-conserving surgery followed by whole-breast radiotherapy yields overall survival equivalent to total mastectomy
Sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) utilizes dual tracers (technetium-99m colloid and blue dye) to stage the axilla with low morbidity
The ACOSOG Z0011 trial showed that completion axillary dissection can be safely omitted in patients with 1-2 positive sentinel nodes undergoing lumpectomy and whole-breast radiation
HER2-positive breast cancer requires anti-HER2 monoclonal antibodies (trastuzumab and pertuzumab) alongside systemic chemotherapy
Tamoxifen is the endocrine adjuvant therapy of choice in premenopausal hormone-receptor positive patients, whereas aromatase inhibitors are preferred in postmenopausal patients
reference.pathophysiology: Invasive breast carcinoma arises from ductal or lobular epithelium through progressive accumulation of somatic genetic alterations (TP53, PIK3CA, HER2 amplification) and epigenetic modifications. Molecular classification stratifies tumors into Luminal A (ER+/PR+/HER2-, low Ki-67), Luminal B (ER+/PR variable/HER2 variable, high proliferation), HER2-enriched, and Triple-Negative (basal-like). Tumor cells invade the basement membrane, infiltrate stroma, and disseminate via lymphatic channels to axillary lymph nodes and hematogenously to bone, liver, lungs, and brain.
additionalDifferentials: Invasive ductal carcinoma of no special type versus invasive lobular carcinoma with E-cadherin loss
Inflammatory breast cancer versus severe bacterial cellulitis or mastitis
Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) with microinvasion versus high-grade comedo DCIS
Medullary breast carcinoma versus poorly differentiated high-grade invasive ductal carcinoma
additionalInvestigations: Digital bilateral mammography and targeted breast and axillary ultrasonography
Core needle biopsy for histological confirmation, Nottingham grading, and ER, PR, HER2, and Ki-67 profiling
Contrast-enhanced dynamic breast MRI for evaluating occult multifocality in invasive lobular cancer or dense breast tissue
Contrast-enhanced CT of chest, abdomen, and pelvis plus bone scintigraphy for systemic staging in Stage III or symptomatic patients
